alex: Hey team — customer (acme-inc) says their user can't open Project "Acme Payments" in the Console. They get a 403 Permission Denied when clicking into the project settings. Repro steps they sent:
1) SSO login via Okta -> success
2) Visit https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/projects/acme-payments -> 403 page
3) Tried incognito and different browser -> same

Response they pasted:
```
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"User does not have permission to access project: acme-payments","status":403}
```
They say the user is in the "acme-admins" Okta group which should map to Org Admin. UI shows them as "Member" when we impersonate. Need quick triage — is this role sync, a missing group mapping, or a Console bug? Can someone look at role mapping for acme org id org_9Xc? @maria can you escalate if needed?

jess: FYI from product: mapping precedence is: 1) direct project assignment, 2) org-level direct role, 3) SSO group claims at token time, 4) SCIM-provisioned groups (applied by background job). That means if token didn't include the acme-admins claim at auth time, they might be member until next login or token refresh. We built that to avoid instant privilege escalation via SCIM.

maria: Ok that explains it. Customer logged in before the SCIM job applied. Two mitigations: 1) Ask user to log out and log back in, OR 2) Support can trigger a session refresh for that user (we have an endpoint). Command: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/sessions/refresh -d '{"user_id":"usr_ABC"}'`

alex: I ran the refresh endpoint. Support output:
```
{"status":"ok","refreshed":1}
```
Rechecked effective-roles:
```
{"user_id":"usr_ABC","org_id":"org_9Xc","effective_roles":["org_admin"],"direct_project_roles":[]}
```
Customer confirmed they can access the project now. I'll reply with root cause: SCIM background job applied groups after the user's session token was minted; token-time group claims take precedence, so they needed to re-auth. I'll include the workaround and note for product to consider reducing session refresh friction.
